card: This PR hardens the read-only BDB wallet parser against crafted files that cause infinite loops, exponential traversal time, or huge memory inflation. It tracks visited B-tree and overflow pages to prevent cyclic or multi-parent graph traversal, and validates that internal records, data records, and overflow page data do not exceed page bounds. The author demonstrates that on master an ~8 KB crafted file hangs indefinitely and a 256 KB file balloons memory consumption to ~800 MB. Hand-crafted raw BDB unit tests and fuzz target updates are included.
changed_since_previous: Added a check in OverflowPage::Unserialize and the fuzz target to reject overflow pages where data length exceeds the page size minus the header, along with unit tests for oversized and full overflow pages.
evidence: PR description: 'On master an ~8 KB file built this way [multi-parent btree child] doesn't finish.'
PR description: 'A single 64 KB page can turn into ~500 MB this way. On master a 256 KB file took migratewallet from 54 MB to ~800 MB.'
problem: Malformed BDB files passed to `migratewallet` (RPC/GUI) or `bitcoin-wallet` can trigger infinite loops, exponential DFS execution time, or extreme memory inflation. B-tree pages reachable via multiple paths multiply parsing work exponentially, cyclic chains of zero-length overflow pages bypass length-based loop detection, and overlapping index entries or oversized overflow data offsets can inflate memory usage far beyond the file's size.

risk.why: A false positive in the parser validation could cause valid legacy BDB wallets to fail migration, leaving users unable to access their wallets on modern versions.

summary: Hardens the read-only Berkeley DB parser used during wallet migration against crafted database files. It tracks visited B-tree and overflow pages to reject multi-parent DAG traversal and empty overflow page loops, bounds the sum of record lengths on a page to the page size, and rejects overflow pages whose claimed data length exceeds page bounds. It also adds tests building raw BDB files byte-by-byte and updates the BDB fuzz target with the new and previously missing error strings.
